title: Adjectives II: Collocations
description: Build natural adjective–noun combinations and distinguish near-synonyms.
objectives: Replace vague adjectives with precise ones

source.title: Advanced Grammar & Vocabulary — Express Publishing
source.note: Lesson explanations, examples and practice have been adapted for independent study from the supplied unit. Answers and explanations are editorial, not a publisher answer key.

lessons.title: Learn words in partnerships
lessons.body: A collocation is a combination that sounds natural to proficient speakers. Knowing a definition is not enough: learn an adjective with two or three common nouns.

lessons.title: Before or after a noun
lessons.body: Adjectives often appear before nouns and after linking verbs, but fixed combinations can strongly favour one position. The source highlights typical collocations; these are usage patterns rather than absolute bans in every context.

lessons.title: Close meanings, different uses
lessons.body: Lax describes weak rules or enforcement; lenient describes a person who gives a mild punishment. Harrowing describes a distressing experience or account, rather than a distressed person.
examples: a harrowing documentary; an upset viewer

lessons.title: Precision and register
lessons.body: Mundane suggests ordinary routine; tedious suggests something long and tiresome; dreary adds a depressing quality. Lousy is informal. Choose the word that expresses your meaning and suits the situation.

lessons.title: Using stronger descriptions
lessons.body: Do not replace simple words mechanically. Perfect can become flawless for a performance, impeccable for manners or taste, and unblemished for a record. Context decides which collocation fits.

exerciseGroups.title: Upgrade a film review
exerciseGroups.instruction: Replace the general adjective with a more precise word. More than one answer can work.

questions.explanation: Run-of-the-mill means unremarkable; the other answers can describe conventional style.

questions.prompt: The relatives were bad and unpleasant: their behaviour was ___.
questions.explanation: All mean very bad; lousy is informal.

questions.prompt: Learning these skills was a difficult task: an ___ task.
questions.explanation: Arduous stresses sustained effort.

questions.prompt: The clever professor made an ___ decision.
questions.explanation: Astute describes accurate judgement; “an” also gives a clue.

questions.prompt: The cast gave perfect performances: ___ performances.
questions.explanation: Both can describe performances without faults.

questions.prompt: There was never a boring moment: never a ___ moment.
questions.explanation: “Never a dull moment” is a common expression.

questions.explanation: Gruelling describes a demanding experience, such as a race or schedule.

A performance can have no faults.
Scruffy describes shabby clothes.
A plan can be cunning.
Shrewd describes practical judgement.
Exercise can demand great physical effort.
For this unit, use tedious task or dull room; tedious typically describes an activity or experience.
A driver can be extremely bad at driving.
This can mean a look suggesting perceptiveness; context matters.
A journey can require sustained effort.

Mainstream describes widely accepted political positions.

exerciseGroups.title: Vocabulary recall
exerciseGroups.instruction: Choose the word or phrase that matches the meaning.

questions.explanation: She is an avid reader of biographies. Common: reader, fan, collector.

questions.prompt: Very obvious and without shame, usually something bad.
questions.explanation: It was a blatant lie. Common: lie, foul, disregard.
The mountain view was breathtaking. Common: view, scenery.

questions.prompt: So exciting that it holds your attention.
questions.explanation: We watched a gripping thriller. Common: film, tale, novel.
The documentary contained harrowing accounts. Describes an experience or account.
Lax security allowed strangers inside. Common: security, discipline, enforcement.

questions.prompt: Giving a less severe punishment than expected.
questions.explanation: The lenient judge issued a warning. Often describes judges, parents or teachers.
The actor enjoyed a meteoric rise. Common: rise to fame.
The advertisement was misleading. Common: information, comments, advertising.

questions.prompt: Very high and loud, especially a sound.
questions.explanation: A piercing scream broke the silence. Common: scream, whistle.

questions.prompt: Producing a large amount of creative work.
questions.explanation: The prolific novelist publishes every year. Common: writer, composer, artist.
Sporadic fighting continued near the border. Common: fighting, outbreaks, showers.
He remained a staunch ally. Common: supporter, friend, ally.

questions.prompt: Broad and general, or affecting many things.
questions.explanation: The proposal introduced sweeping changes. Common: generalisation, reforms, changes.

questions.prompt: So sound that it is difficult to challenge.
questions.explanation: Her argument was watertight. Common: alibi, case, argument.

questions.prompt: Of a very high standard, without faults.
